concept.name: Midpoint peg order
concept.definition: A pegged order whose working price tracks the midpoint of the national best bid and offer, so executions occur halfway between the displayed bid and ask. It is typically non-displayed and is used to capture half the spread relative to crossing it.
concept.intuition: It is a standing offer to trade 'at the halfway mark': both sides split the spread instead of one side paying it.
concept.mechanics: The venue continuously re-prices the order to the NBBO midpoint as quotes move; the order rests non-displayed and executes only when contra-side interest (often a market or marketable order) is willing to trade at the midpoint. Exchange protocols denote it as a midpoint peg instruction (e.g., Cboe ExecInst M).
concept.formula: Working price = (national best bid + national best offer) / 2.
concept.failure_modes: When the NBBO is locked or crossed the midpoint is unstable, and some venues suspend midpoint matching in those states. Midpoint orders are also adversely selected: they tend to fill just before the quote moves against the resting side.
concept.misconceptions: A midpoint peg does not guarantee a better net price than a market order once missed fills and adverse selection are counted; and the 'midpoint' is the NBBO midpoint, not the midpoint of any single venue's book.
concept.example: NBBO is $20.00 x $20.04; your midpoint-pegged sell rests at $20.02 (non-displayed) and executes when a buy order sweeps through, saving $0.02 versus hitting the bid.

citations.source: Cboe Titanium U.S. Equities BOE Specification
citations.section: ExecInst M = Midpoint (peg to NBBO Midpoint)
